output.title: Expedited Prior Authorization Decision Timeframe
output.draft_text:
Q: How long does an expedited prior authorization decision take?

A: When a prior authorization request qualifies for expedited (urgent) review, a decision is made within [expedited decision timeframe, e.g., number of hours] of receiving [the complete request / all required information from the prescriber]. Expedited review applies when [criteria for expedited review, e.g., the prescriber indicates that waiting for a standard decision could seriously jeopardize the member's life, health, or ability to regain maximum function]. For comparison, standard (non-urgent) prior authorization requests are decided within [standard decision timeframe].

How to request expedited review: [who can request expedited review, e.g., prescriber and/or member] can request it by [submission method(s), e.g., phone, fax, electronic PA portal] at [contact/phone/fax number]. [Whether prescriber attestation or supporting documentation is required.]

If the request does not qualify as expedited: [what happens, e.g., the request is moved to standard review and the member/prescriber is notified within [notification timeframe] by [notification method]].

If additional information is needed: [whether the clock pauses or extends, and any allowed extension period].

How the decision is communicated: The decision is sent to [recipients, e.g., prescriber and member] by [method(s)] within [notification timeframe]. If the request is denied, the member may [appeal options, including expedited appeal and its timeframe].

If no decision is made within the required timeframe: [what happens, e.g., escalation path or member rights].

Advocate tip: [any interim supply or emergency fill option available while the expedited request is pending, if applicable].
placeholders: [expedited decision timeframe, e.g., number of hours]
[the complete request / all required information from the prescriber]
[whether prescriber attestation or supporting documentation is required]
[what happens if the request does not qualify as expedited]
[whether the clock pauses or extends, and any allowed extension period]
[appeal options, including expedited appeal and its timeframe]
[what happens if no decision is made within the required timeframe]
[any interim supply or emergency fill option available]
author_checklist: Confirm the exact expedited PA decision timeframe and its units (hours vs. calendar/business days).
Confirm when the clock starts (receipt of request vs. receipt of all required clinical information).
Confirm whether timeframes differ by line of business (e.g., commercial, Medicare Part D, Medicaid, ERISA plans) or by state, and specify which plans this unit covers.
Confirm the criteria that qualify a request for expedited review and who determines eligibility.
Confirm who may request expedited review (prescriber, member, authorized representative) and accepted submission channels and contact details.
Confirm the standard PA decision timeframe for comparison.
Confirm whether extensions are allowed when information is missing and the maximum extension period.
Confirm how and to whom decisions are communicated and the notification deadline.
Confirm the process when an expedited request is downgraded to standard review.
Confirm appeal rights after denial, including expedited appeal timeframes.
Confirm whether an interim or emergency supply is available while a decision is pending; remove the tip if not.
Verify all timeframes against current regulatory requirements and plan documents, and cite the source documents.
Remove any placeholder sections that do not apply before approval.
